repair.title: Compare the familiar words
repair.body: Italian has five vowel letters: a, e, i, o, u. Keep vowel sounds clear when you imitate the examples. E and o each have open and closed pronunciations; spelling alone does not always tell you which. Many familiar words stress the second-to-last syllable, as in casa, but this is not a rule for every word. A written final accent marks final stress: città, caffè.

examples.en: A coffee in town.

Anna: “I am going to a party. Why don’t you come too?”

Luca: “At seven.”

units.title: Prepositions and articles
units.description: Join a and di to every article, including clock times and whose something is.

lessons.title: Join a to every article
lessons.outcome: I can choose al, allo, all’, alla, ai, agli or alle from the noun’s article, and say clock times.
lessons.takeaway: A joins the article of the noun: al mercato, allo stadio, all’ospedale, alla stazione, ai genitori, agli studenti, alle amiche. Clock hours take alle (alle otto), one o’clock takes all’una, and mezzogiorno and mezzanotte take a alone.
